answer: A reputation bond works like a glacier: slow to build, hard to fake. Each agent stakes value that only accrues through verified work over time, so a fresh fake identity starts with zero standing and must pay real compute and time before it can transact. Like an ember that needs steady fuel, trust grows only from sustained honest service, while a meadow of many small independent attestations makes one forged identity worthless - an attacker must buy the whole field, not plant a single seed.
